newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Woman enters race to be Euro-parliament president.
newsitem.headline: Woman enters race to be Euro-parliament president.

text.p: A late French challenger emerged on Thursday for the post of European Parliament president, although a Spanish candidate backed by the assembly's two biggest groups is virtually certain to win.

Catherine Lalumiere, a former Council of Europe Secretary General, said she was standing to protest at what she said was a vote decided in advance by the big Socialist and Christian Democrat groups under a long-standing deal.
These two groups back Spain's Partido Popular deputy Jose-Maria Gil-Robles, whose election is assured in Tuesday's vote in Strasbourg.
Lalumiere, a former French European Affairs Minister and leader of the alternative European Radical Alliance group, said smaller groups saw the vote as undemocratic.
"This procedure excludes the smaller EU member states and the small parliamentary groups," she said in a statement.
Parliamentary officials say Lalumiere could garner around 100 of the parliament's 626 votes, with many deputies from the smaller groups backing her.

"She is more than a symbolic candidate," German leader of the Greens Claudia Roth told Reuters by telephone, saying she had European experience and that "after years and years and years of men it would be a good thing to have a woman."
"All the arguments are for her," Roth said.
The president of the parliament's Liberal Group, Dutchman Gijs De Vries, said his group would back Lalumiere.
"It demonstrates our deep dissatisfaction at the undemocratic procedure used by the Socialists and Christian Democrats," he told Reuters by telephone.
The European Parliament is the EU's directly elected assembly.
